A customer has many orders.
Book: title, author, year of publication.
One author writes several books.
Entities: student, group, teacher.
A department has many employees. An employee has a name, a position and a salary.
A student takes many courses, and many students attend a course.
An order contains many items. An item has a quantity and a price. A customer places many orders.
A doctor sees many patients. A patient has many appointments. Each appointment is assigned by one doctor.
Tables: product (name, price), category (name). A category has many products.
A user writes many comments. An article contains many comments.
A shop sells many products. A supplier supplies several products.
A user has a login, a password and an email.
A student enrolls in many courses, and each course has many students. A student has a name and a number. A teacher teaches several courses. A course has a title and a number of hours.
Library: reader, book, loan. A reader makes many loans, a book takes part in many loans.
A country includes many cities. A city has many streets.
Online shop. A buyer (name, address) places many orders. An order (date, total) contains many products, and a product (name, price) is part of many orders. A product belongs to one category.
A musician records many albums.
A film has a title and a year. A cinema shows many sessions. A session belongs to one film.
Entities: project, task, employee. A project has a name and a deadline. A project contains many tasks. One employee performs a task, and an employee has many tasks.
A group has several students.
A hotel contains many rooms. A guest books many rooms. A booking links a guest and a room.
Product: id, name, price, quantity in stock.
An actor stars in many films, and a film has many actors.
Bank: a client (full name, phone) opens several accounts. An account (number, balance) has many transactions. A transaction (date, amount) belongs to one account.
A teacher gives many subjects. A subject belongs to a curriculum.
A publisher issues many books.
A tag (name) can belong to many articles, an article (title, text) has many tags. An author (name) writes many articles. An article does not have several authors.
A customer has many addresses. An address belongs to one customer.
Warehouse: entities warehouse, product, batch. A warehouse contains many batches. A batch consists of one product. A batch has a quantity and an arrival date. One product arrives in many batches.
A class includes many pupils.
The user sends a request to the server. The server returns a response to the user.
The client calls the service, the service replies to the client.
The browser sends a request to the server. The server queries the database. The database returns data to the server. The server responds to the browser.
The buyer selects an item in the shop. The shop requests payment from the bank. The bank confirms the payment to the shop. The shop sends the buyer a receipt.
The app sends a message to the notification server, the notification server delivers the notification to the user.
The student sends an application to the dean office. The dean office checks the application in the system. The system returns the result to the dean office. The dean office notifies the student.
The client asks the ATM for the balance. The ATM calls the bank. The bank returns the balance to the ATM. The ATM shows the balance to the client.

The user opens the app. The app sends the login and password to the auth server. The auth server checks the password in the user database. The database returns the result. The auth server issues a token to the app. The app shows the home page to the user.
The sender passes the letter to the mail server. The mail server delivers the letter to the recipient.
The dispatcher calls the driver. The driver confirms the call to the dispatcher. The dispatcher tells the passenger the arrival time.

The client places an order in the online shop. The shop checks stock at the warehouse. The warehouse confirms availability. The shop creates a payment in the payment system. The payment system asks the bank for confirmation. The bank confirms. The payment system reports success to the shop. The shop sends the client an order confirmation.
The camera sends a picture to the server. The server saves the picture to the storage.
The frontend requests the product list from the API. The API reads the products from the database. The database gives the products to the API. The API returns the list to the frontend.
The doctor sends a referral to the laboratory. The laboratory sends the results to the doctor. The doctor tells the patient the diagnosis.

The mobile app asks the gateway for the weather. The gateway checks the cache. The cache returns an empty answer to the gateway. The gateway requests data from the weather service. The weather service returns a forecast to the gateway. The gateway writes the forecast to the cache and sends it to the app.
The waiter passes the order to the cook. The cook returns the finished dish to the waiter.
The user presses the pay button. The payment page calls the payment gateway. The payment gateway answers the payment page. The payment page shows the result to the user.

The client submits the registration form to the server. The server checks the email in the database. The database tells the server the email already exists. The server does not create the user and returns an error to the client.
The reader asks the librarian for a book. The librarian hands the book to the reader.
The order service publishes an event to the broker. The broker delivers the event to the warehouse service. The warehouse service sends a confirmation to the order service.

The passenger orders a taxi in the app. The app sends the order to the dispatch server. The dispatch server finds a driver and sends them an offer. The driver accepts the offer. The dispatch server tells the app the driver details. The app shows the passenger the car and the time.
The sensor sends readings to the controller. The controller turns on the fan.
The administrator creates an account in the system. The system emails a password to the user. The user confirms the login to the system.
The website requests the exchange rate from the rates service. The rates service returns the rate to the website.

The terminal sends the card to processing for verification. Processing queries the bank. The bank declines the operation because of insufficient funds. Processing reports the refusal to the terminal. The terminal does not print a receipt and shows the refusal to the cashier.
The printer asks the print server for a job. The print server sends the job to the printer.
The teacher uploads grades to the register. The register notifies the parent. The parent confirms reading to the register.

The user picks a file and presses upload. The client sends the file to the server. The server scans the file with the antivirus. The antivirus returns a verdict to the server. The server stores the file in the cloud. The cloud confirms the save. The server answers the client with a link to the file.
The buyer asks the seller for a discount. The seller asks the manager for permission. The manager allows it to the seller. The seller tells the buyer the new price.
The guest knocks on the door. The host opens the door to the guest.
The customer sends order data to the order entry process. The order entry process saves the order to the orders data store.
The verification process reads data from the users database and passes the result to the administrator.
The buyer sends payment data to the payment process. The payment process writes the payment to the payments store and sends a receipt to the buyer.
Data from sensors goes to the collection process. The collection process writes readings to the archive. The analysis process reads the archive and gives a report to the operator.
The student sends an application to the registration process, which returns an application number to the student.
The supplier sends a delivery note to the receiving process. Receiving checks the note against data from the orders store and writes stock levels to the warehouse store.

The patient gives complaints to the intake process. The intake process takes the medical history from the card file and gives a summary to the doctor. The doctor writes the diagnosis to the card file.
The accounting process writes purchases to the sales log.

The customer sends an order to the order processing process. Processing checks the customer in the customer base, reserves the goods in the warehouse base and passes the order to the delivery process. The delivery process gives the courier a route. The courier returns a delivery mark to order processing.
The tax service sends a request to the report preparation process. Preparation collects the data and sends the report back to the tax service.
The bank passes a statement to the import process, and the import process saves the operations to the transactions database.
The visitor enters a search query into the search process. The search process reads the index and returns results to the visitor. The logging process writes queries to the log.

The teacher enters grades into the grading sheet process. The sheet saves the grades to the performance database. The scholarship process reads the performance database and passes a list of recipients to accounting. The student asks the sheet process for their grades and receives a transcript.
The employee enters a time report into the timesheet process.
The subscription process receives an email from the visitor and adds it to the mailing list. The mailing process reads the list and sends letters to subscribers.
The warehouse passes stock data to the sync process. Sync updates the product catalog. The shop receives the updated catalog.

The applicant sends documents to the verification process. Verification compares the documents with the registry and, if there are no matches, passes them to the registration process. Registration writes the decision to the registry and sends a notification to the applicant.
The ordering process reads prices from the price list.
The administrator sends settings to the configuration process. Configuration sends a confirmation to the administrator and passes the settings to the apply process.

The buyer places an order through the sales process. Sales writes the order to the orders database and requests payment from the payment process. The payment process contacts the bank, gets a reply and writes the result to the payments database. Sales receives the payment status and sends a receipt to the buyer.
The librarian enters a new book into the catalog.
The reporting process collects data from the sales store and the returns store and sends a summary report to the director.

The subscriber pays for a service in the billing process. Billing reads the tariff from the tariffs database and charges the account in the accounts database. The notification process reads the accounts database and sends the subscriber a low balance message.
The client sends a technical specification to the estimation process.
The import process loads products from the supplier file into the catalog. The publishing process reads the catalog and sends the products to the website.
The guard passes visitor information to the registration process, which keeps records in the visit log.

Support receives a ticket from the customer in the intake process. Intake writes the ticket to the tickets database and passes it to the routing process. Routing reads the staff database and sends the ticket to an engineer. The engineer writes the solution to the tickets database, and the notification process sends the customer a reply.
The voting process writes votes to the ballots store.
The driver sends coordinates to the tracking process, which passes the current position to the dispatcher.
The customer sends a complaint to the complaint handling process, which returns a reply to the customer.
